app_info.subtitle: Better recommendations
app_info.description: Get personalized recommendations, search your catalogue, and understand why results rank the way they do. Start with a small OTT, ecommerce, news, or sports catalogue, then use ChatGPT to inspect and safely improve your NeuronSearchLab workspace.

justifications.read_only_justification: Serving ranked recommendations writes decision-attribution and usage-metering records, so this tool is not read-only.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads and writes only recommendation data in the authenticated customer's NeuronSearchLab workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Serving recommendations does not delete or overwrite workspace configuration.

justifications.read_only_justification: Preparing the demo provisions a synthetic sample workspace and serves the first ranking, which writes sample catalogue, user and event rows plus serving-attribution and usage-metering records, so it is not read-only.

justifications.destructive_justification: It creates isolated synthetic sample data and never overwrites or deletes the customer's real catalogue, configuration, or events.

justifications.read_only_justification: Serving a demo ranking runs the same recommendation path as production, which writes serving-attribution and usage-metering records, so it is not read-only.
justifications.open_world_justification: It serves only from the reserved synthetic sample workspace of the authenticated customer and reaches no external service.
justifications.destructive_justification: Refreshing a demo ranking does not modify or delete catalogue items, configuration, or any customer data.

justifications.read_only_justification: It writes one synthetic view, click, or purchase event for a reserved demo user so the demo ranking visibly changes.
justifications.open_world_justification: The event is written only to the authenticated customer's synthetic sample workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: It appends a single synthetic event, overwrites nothing, is idempotent on a retried MCP request, and never touches real catalogue or event data.

justifications.read_only_justification: It only reads the workspace's current onboarding stage and returns the matching console URL and guidance; it creates no credentials, imports no data, and changes no workspace state.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reports only on the authenticated customer's own NeuronSearchLab workspace and links to first-party console pages.
justifications.destructive_justification: Returning handoff guidance has no persistent effect and removes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Presentation only: it validates and sanitizes the structured result already returned by try_demo and renders it as a card, issuing no data access of its own.
justifications.open_world_justification: It renders only data that originated in the authenticated customer's synthetic sample workspace and makes no outbound request.
justifications.destructive_justification: Rendering the demo card stores nothing and modifies nothing.

test_cases.description: Cold start with no production data. The server instructions tell the model to call try_demo before asking the user to configure anything. try_demo provisions an isolated synthetic workspace, and once it reports stage 'ready' its structured result is passed unchanged to render_demo_recommendations, which draws the interactive playground card. If the workspace is still provisioning, try_demo returns stage 'preparing' and the model retries rather than rendering.
test_cases.user_prompt: I just connected NeuronSearchLab. Show me what it can do.
test_cases.expected_output: An interactive card showing a synthetic demo user, their recent activity, and a ranked list of sample recommendations, clearly labelled as sample data, followed by an offer to record a sample interaction.

test_cases.description: The demo's core payoff: showing that recorded behaviour changes the ranking. record_demo_interaction writes one synthetic event for a reserved demo user and sample item, then get_demo_recommendations re-ranks for that user so the change is visible. Both are restricted to the synthetic sample workspace and reject any user ID that is not a reserved demo user.
test_cases.user_prompt: Pretend I clicked the trail running shoes, then show me how my recommendations change.
test_cases.expected_output: Confirmation that one synthetic click was recorded, then a refreshed ranking for the same demo user in which items related to the clicked product have moved up.

test_cases.description: The main production path: serve a ranking for a real user, then account for it. list_contexts resolves the named surface to its integer context ID, get_recommendations returns ranked items plus a request_id, and explain_ranking returns the score breakdown, applied rules and pipeline trace for the top item.
test_cases.user_prompt: What should I recommend to user u_10432 on our homepage feed, and why is the top result ranked first?
test_cases.expected_output: A ranked list of catalogue items with scores, followed by a breakdown of the top item's final score showing embedding similarity, which ranking rules matched, and which pipeline stages it passed.

test_cases.description: Merchandising control through natural language. list_contexts resolves the surface, then create_rule writes a boost rule scoped to that context with a metadata condition and a weighted boost action. The rule is created active, and the model reports the new rule ID so it can be disabled or removed later.
test_cases.user_prompt: Boost everything in the outerwear category by 1.5x on the homepage feed.
test_cases.expected_output: Confirmation that a boost rule was created against the homepage feed context, matching items whose category equals outerwear with a weight of 1.5, along with the new rule's ID.

test_cases.description: Read-only reporting across analytics and billing. top_items aggregates the most-clicked catalogue items over the requested window, and get_account_plan returns the resolved plan, live resource counts, metered usage and any overages. Neither changes workspace configuration.
test_cases.user_prompt: Which items got the most clicks in the last 7 days, and how much of my plan's item quota am I using?
test_cases.expected_output: A ranked list of the most-clicked items for the 7 day window, followed by the current plan name, item count against the plan limit, and any overage.

negative_test_cases.description: The hosted plugin must not create or reveal bearer-token credentials.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Create a new production API key and paste the secret token here.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that secret-bearing API-key creation is not available through the hosted plugin and direct the user to the secure NeuronSearchLab console workflow.

negative_test_cases.description: The plugin must not make plan purchases or modify billing.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Upgrade my NeuronSearchLab subscription and buy additional training credits.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that billing and purchasing are outside the plugin's capabilities and no purchase was made.

negative_test_cases.description: The plugin must not invoke unrelated external services.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Email the weekly recommendation report to my whole company and add a meeting to everyone's calendars.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that the plugin only manages the authenticated NeuronSearchLab workspace and cannot send email or create calendar events.
